Components / Surfaces

Cover card

.dr-card--cover · .dr-well--photo · .dr-listing__foot · __body · __name · __desc · .dr-btn--onphoto · components/card.css · kit specimen

Anatomy

Video 0:38 · 46 MB
  1. 1.dr-card--coverThe card with no inset: padding 0, gap 0, overflow:hidden, clipped by its own radius 16. No shadow.
  2. 2.dr-well--photoThe cover, 180 tall, flush to three edges. The media's 13 radius is switched off, so one corner carries one radius.
  3. 3.dr-btn--onphotoThe play button on the photograph, a 44 × 44 grey disc centred on the cover, its name in aria-label; see Circular action.
  4. 4.dr-listing__footThe file's line, 68 tall at padding 12 / 16, gap 12.
  5. 5.dr-listing__nameThe file's kind, Video, 15/600 in --text-primary, 14.37:1. The size and length under it are 13/400 in --text-muted, 5.95:1.
  6. 6.dr-listing__foot .dr-btn--iconThe file's action, Download video, a grey 44 × 44 icon button with its name in aria-label.

Variants and sizes

Inventory rows: Cover card.

States

No state of its own: the card is a surface and not a link, so nothing in it takes focus but its two discs. Play and Download take the circular action states.

When to use

The cover card holds one file of an aerial delivery where the picture is the content: one user, the video card on order-details-aerial. A cover is never inset, and that is the imagery rule winning where it meets the inset rule: a photograph is the surface, and a picture floated inside a padded card is the sticker the rule forbids. The padding moves onto the line below, 12 vertical against 16 horizontal, because that line already carries a 44px control and its height is set by the target.

Both actions are icon buttons, not pills, 44 × 44 with an aria-label each. WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name stops applying rather than failing, since there is no visible label to contain. They are grey, not green: Book again is that screen's one green control. Two files in one zone are told apart by what they show, not by a badge, and the alt describes the frame and only the frame. The action word is still Download, spoken instead of printed.

Sources: DESIGN.md § Cards (.dr-card--cover) · § Imagery · inventory.md § 1.3 (Cover card) · voice.md Vocabulary · ui/kit.html Cover card

Rule and anti-rule

Do

Video 0:38 · 46 MB

A photograph that is the deliverable runs to the card's edges, and the file's facts and action sit on the line beneath it.

Don’t

Video 0:38 · 46 MB

A photograph inset inside a padded card: a sticker on a card, with two radii on nested corners. Take the padding off with --cover. A transparent drone cutout is the opposite case and sits in a plain media well on an ordinary card.
